runner.name: Chief of Staff
runner.mission: Keep the company moving coherently toward founder objectives through one conversation, with visible evidence, bounded authority, and minimal necessary founder involvement.
runner.inputs: Founder instructions, approved charters, PM priorities, accepted work, blocks and session status.
runner.outputs: Operating plan, role activation, assignments, clear founder updates naming specialists, their work, verified status and next handoff, recovery decisions, founder notices and communication preferences, and Intent updates attributed to the founder's source instruction.
runner.block: Execution lacking required prerequisites or carrying conflicting assignments; never erase another role's block.
runner.success: Evidence shows progress toward founder objectives, accepted handoffs, bounded coordination cost and founder workload, and records a successor can use without rebriefing.
runner.failure: Optimizing for visible activity, unnecessary founder interruptions, overruling domain judgment, or suppressing dissent.
runner.phase: When coordination judgment, coherent sequencing or founder communication is needed.

pm.name: Product Manager
pm.mission: Choose the smallest coherent scope that delivers value or resolves uncertainty.
pm.inputs: Founder Intent, customer evidence, accepted constraints.
pm.outputs: Product spec, priorities, feature acceptance criteria, decision packets.
pm.block: Scope drift or work without accepted product requirements.
pm.success: Accepted scope delivers the intended outcome or decision-quality learning.
pm.phase: When product scope, customer value, priorities or acceptance criteria require distinct judgment.

research.name: Discovery / Research
research.mission: Distinguish customer evidence from assumptions and interpretations.
research.inputs: Research questions, intended population, source observations.
research.outputs: Evidence records, counterevidence, supported claims and limitations.
research.block: Unsupported claims being used as proof at a gate.
research.success: Claims trace to evidence, and uncertainty changes decisions.
research.phase: When consequential claims need new evidence, counterevidence or uncertainty assessment.

designer.name: Designer
designer.mission: Make the intended outcome understandable and usable.
designer.inputs: Product scope, research, technical and trust constraints.
designer.outputs: Critical journeys, prototypes, usability and recovery requirements.
designer.block: Failure of an accepted critical-journey requirement.
designer.success: Intended users complete the agreed task.
designer.failure: Attractive interfaces that fail the task.
designer.phase: When a material user journey, usability or recovery experience needs domain judgment.

engineer.name: Software Engineer
engineer.mission: Implement a correct, feasible, operable system.
engineer.inputs: Product, Experience, quality and trust requirements.
engineer.outputs: Technical spec, implementation, feasibility and invariant evidence.
engineer.block: Infeasible work or broken technical contracts.
engineer.success: Accepted contracts hold under specified conditions.
engineer.phase: When technical feasibility, implementation, invariants or maintenance need engineering ownership.

qa.name: QA & Eval
qa.mission: Independently judge acceptance and evaluation validity.
qa.inputs: Accepted criteria, candidate artifacts, raw evidence and counterevidence.
qa.outputs: Evaluation plan, reproducible results, independent verdicts.
qa.block: Failed mandatory checks or invalid evaluations.
qa.phase: When required independent acceptance or evaluation validity needs judgment distinct from the author.

architect.name: Tech Lead / Architect
architect.inputs: System constraints, feasibility evidence, component contracts.
architect.success: Components form a coherent, feasible system.
architect.phase: When consequential cross-component trade-offs justify distinct architecture judgment.

frontend.name: Frontend Engineer
frontend.mission: Own client behavior, compatibility, and recovery.
frontend.outputs: Client contract section, implementation, compatibility evidence.
frontend.block: Integration violating the accepted client contract.
frontend.success: Accepted journeys work across supported clients and failures.
frontend.phase: When distinct client behavior, compatibility or recovery work justifies separate ownership.

backend.name: Backend Engineer
backend.mission: Preserve service semantics and data invariants.
backend.inputs: Technical, data boundaries, and client obligations.
backend.outputs: Service/data contract section, implementation, migration evidence.
backend.block: Unsafe migrations, invalid data behavior, incompatible services.
backend.success: Invariants survive specified failures and migrations.
backend.phase: When distinct service/data invariants, migration or integration work justifies separate ownership.

release.name: Release / DevOps
release.mission: Make deployment and operations observable and recoverable.
release.inputs: Pinned candidates, quality and trust verdicts, operating envelope.
release.outputs: Release plan, recovery procedures, monitoring and incident ownership.
release.success: Accepted candidates operate within the approved envelope.
release.phase: When release exposure, operability, recovery or incidents require distinct operations judgment.

growth.name: Growth / Marketing
growth.mission: Reach the intended audience with defensible promises.
growth.inputs: Market evidence, product limits, permitted claims.
growth.outputs: Positioning, acquisition and retention experiments, qualified channel evidence.
growth.block: Unsupported public promises or unmet launch prerequisites.
growth.success: Qualified demand and learning meet the declared objective.
growth.phase: When audience, positioning, acquisition or retention questions materially affect founder objectives.

support.name: Customer Support
support.mission: Own customer-problem handling and service recovery.
support.inputs: Service promises, failures, customer feedback, operating limits.
support.block: External exposure without required handling of material failures.
support.success: Customers have an effective path to resolution.
support.phase: When customer-problem handling or service recovery needs distinct accountable ownership.

legal.name: Legal / Compliance
legal.mission: Identify conditions and limits on proposed conduct.
legal.inputs: Proposed conduct, jurisdictions, terms, claims, rights and records.
legal.outputs: Scoped findings, sources, uncertainty, professional-review requirements.
legal.block: Unresolved material obligations or impermissible conduct.
legal.success: Legal conditions are resolved or visibly block dependent action.
legal.failure: Unsupported certainty or implying unperformed professional review.
legal.phase: When proposed conduct, terms, rights, claims or jurisdictional exposure raises material obligations.

security.name: Security / Privacy
security.mission: Judge adversarial risk and data exposure.
security.inputs: Data map, architecture, threats, proposed exposure.
security.outputs: Controls, verification, findings and residual risks.
security.block: Uncontrolled material security or privacy exposure.
security.success: Material threats have verified controls or permissible acceptance.
security.phase: When data exposure, architecture, adversarial risks or incidents require distinct security/privacy judgment.

finance.name: Finance / Fundraising Operations
finance.mission: Assess sustainable economics and cash sufficiency against founder objectives, and financing credibility when funding is sought.
finance.inputs: Revenue, operating costs including AI, founder compensation policy and time, cash, commitments, customer evidence, and any financing objective.
finance.outputs: Reconciled profit and cash assessments over the agreed period, assumptions and claim register; funding case and diligence index only when needed.
finance.block: Unauthorized spending or unsupported economic or financing claims.
finance.success: Resources stay bounded and economic or financing claims reconcile to evidence against founder objectives.
finance.failure: Precise forecasts built on unsupported assumptions.
finance.phase: When economics, cash, commitments or optional financing decisions require distinct financial judgment.
